text: Ewald summation Ewald summation evaluates periodic Coulomb interactions through complementary real- and reciprocal-space sums. It defines a different boundary-value problem from simply truncating 1/r at a finite radius. Problem and representative equations Consider point charges qᵢ in a neutral, triply periodic cell. Set rᵢⱼₙ=rᵢ−rⱼ+n, cell volume V, splitting parameter α>0 and reciprocal vector k. S(k) is the charge structure factor. The energy below uses unit Coulomb prefactor, omits k=0 and assumes a conducting macroscopic boundary. The prime excludes only i=j,n=0. Restore the same Coulomb prefactor to every term in dimensional units. Changing α redistributes work between sums but cannot change their converged total. Derive forces from the same energy convention. Conditions and pitfalls A net-charged cell requires an additional convention such as a compensating background. Specify potential gauge, surface term, periodic self images and molecular exclusions separately. A periodic gravitational Poisson solve changes the kernel/sign and mean-density treatment; it is not the same calculation. The companion release keeps an asymmetric neutral eight-charge cubic cell, triply periodic with tin-foil boundaries. It separates the direct-Ewald splitting parameter, real-image and reciprocal-cube cutoffs, using a separately implemented heat-kernel theta integral as a reference. It does not extend to charged backgrounds or slabs. What to check For a small neutral configuration, increase both cutoffs independently and test α independence. Compare forces with finite differences of energy, and check translation invariance and net force. Agreement between two unconverged sums is not independent validation. Historical and companion inputs, criteria and results are retained separately. The companion checks energy and every particle force, refinement of the reference integral itself, translations, particle ordering, net force and energy differences individually; a deliberately truncated control is distinct from a converged reference. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Neutral-cell Ewald sums and an independent theta integral Computation for a fixed target Implement real-space, reciprocal-space and self Ewald terms for neutral 3D periodic Coulomb charges; vary splitting and cutoffs. No charged-cell/background correction, triclinic cell, finite-dielectric surface term, slab correction, stress or material-specific force field.
